learn.hook: About 4,500 years ago, people in our part of the world were already living in planned cities with drains. Let's visit them!
points: The Harappan civilisation is one of the world's oldest. It is also called the Indus or Sindhu-Sarasvati civilisation.
It is named after Harappa, the first of its cities to be excavated, in the 1920s. Harappa and Mohenjo-daro are now in Pakistan.
Important Harappan sites in India include Dholavira and Lothal (Gujarat), Kalibangan (Rajasthan) and Rakhigarhi (Haryana).
Its cities were at their peak from about 2600 BCE to about 1900 BCE, along the Sindhu (Indus) river and the Ghaggar-Hakra (often identified with the ancient Sarasvati).
Farmers grew wheat, barley and cotton and kept cattle; skilled crafts-people made pottery, beads, seals and bronze figures.

example.q: Why is it called the 'Harappan' civilisation?
steps: Archaeologists usually name a culture after the first site where it was found.
Harappa was the first city of this civilisation to be excavated.
So the whole civilisation was named after Harappa.
example.answer: Because Harappa was the first of its cities to be excavated.

learn.reallife: You can see real Harappan seals, pots and the famous bronze 'dancing girl' figure in the National Museum, New Delhi.

games.title: Where is this Harappan site today?

quiz.q: Why is this civilisation called 'Harappan'?
options: It had a king named Harappa
Harappa was the first of its cities to be excavated
quiz.explain: Civilisations are often named after the first site found; that was Harappa.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the name comes from a ruler or that Harappa was the only city

quiz.q: Around when were the Harappan cities at their peak?
quiz.explain: The mature (urban) phase of the Harappan civilisation lasted from about 2600 to 1900 BCE.
quiz.mistake: Confuses BCE with CE dates

quiz.q: Which Harappan site is in Gujarat?
quiz.explain: Dholavira is in the Kutch region of Gujarat; Lothal is also in Gujarat.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the states of Harappan sites

quiz.q: Kalibangan, a Harappan site, is in which state?
quiz.explain: Kalibangan lies in Rajasthan, along the Ghaggar river.
quiz.mistake: Confuses Kalibangan with Rakhigarhi

quiz.q: In which present-day country are Harappa and Mohenjo-daro?
quiz.explain: Both these famous cities are in present-day Pakistan.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all Harappan cities are in India

quiz.q: Which crop did Harappan farmers grow?
quiz.explain: Harappans grew wheat, barley and cotton. Potato, tomato and maize came to India much later.
quiz.mistake: Assumes today's common vegetables were always grown here

quiz.q: Rakhigarhi, one of the largest Harappan sites, is in which state?
quiz.explain: Rakhigarhi is in the Hisar district of Haryana.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the states of Harappan sites

quiz.q: The Harappan civilisation is also called by which other name?
quiz.explain: It is called Harappan, Indus or Sindhu-Sarasvati after the river regions where it grew.
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with later kingdoms and empires

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'What was the Harappan civilisation? Where and when did it exist?'
teach.praise: Wow! Harappan cities like Harappa, Mohenjo-daro and Dholavira flourished about 2600 to 1900 BCE. That's ancient!
teach.nudge: When did these cities flourish, and can you name one Harappan city?

learn.hook: Covered drains, straight streets and bathrooms in houses, 4,500 years ago! Harappan engineers were brilliant planners.
points: Harappan cities had straight streets that crossed each other at right angles, in a grid pattern.
Many cities had a raised part called the citadel and a larger lower town where most people lived.
Houses were built of baked bricks of standard sizes. Many houses had a bathroom and some had their own well.
Covered drains ran along the streets to carry dirty water away, a sign of great care for cleanliness.
Mohenjo-daro had the Great Bath, a large, waterproofed tank. Dholavira had large reservoirs to store rainwater.

example.q: Why were Harappan drains covered with bricks or stone?
steps: Open drains can smell bad and spread disease.
Covering them kept dirt and waste out of sight and away from people.
Openings were left so the drains could be cleaned.
example.answer: To keep the city clean and healthy.

learn.reallife: Modern Chandigarh, planned in grids with sectors, follows ideas similar to Harappan town planning!

games.title: Harappan town planning
items: Harappan streets often crossed at right angles.
The cities were laid out like a grid.
Covered drains kept the streets clean.
The Great Bath was found at Mohenjo-daro.
It is one of the best-known Harappan structures.
Harappan houses were mostly made of steel.
They used baked and sun-dried bricks.
Dholavira had reservoirs to store water.
It saved water in a dry region.
Harappan towns had no plan at all.
They were among the best-planned towns of the ancient world.

quiz.q: How were the streets of Harappan cities usually laid out?
options: In a grid, crossing at right angles
quiz.explain: Streets ran straight and crossed each other at right angles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks ancient towns had no planning

quiz.q: What were most Harappan houses built of?
quiz.explain: Harappans used baked (burnt) bricks of standard sizes.
quiz.mistake: Picks a modern material

quiz.q: What did the Harappans build to carry dirty water away?
quiz.explain: Brick-lined covered drains ran along the streets.
quiz.mistake: Does not know about Harappan drainage

quiz.q: Where was the Great Bath found?
quiz.explain: The Great Bath is a large, waterproofed brick tank at Mohenjo-daro.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which structure was at which site

quiz.q: Which Harappan city is famous for its large water reservoirs?
quiz.explain: Dholavira, in dry Kutch, stored rainwater in big reservoirs.
quiz.mistake: Links water storage with the Great Bath

quiz.q: What was the raised, separate part of many Harappan cities called?
quiz.explain: The citadel was built on a higher platform; most people lived in the lower town.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the citadel and the lower town

quiz.q: What does the Harappan drainage system tell us about these people?
options: They cared about cleanliness and health
quiz.explain: Planned, covered drains show great attention to keeping the city clean.
quiz.mistake: Does not draw a conclusion from the evidence

quiz.q: Why is it important that Harappan bricks were of standard sizes across many sites?
options: It shows bricks were made by machines
It means all houses were the same colour
It shows they had no rules
It shows careful planning and shared methods
quiz.explain: Bricks of similar sizes in different cities suggest shared skills and planning.
quiz.mistake: Thinks standard sizes need modern machines

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Were ancient cities just messy villages? What made Harappan towns special?'
teach.praise: Fantastic! Harappan towns had grid streets, covered drains, brick houses, the Great Bath and reservoirs. They were super planners!
teach.nudge: How were the streets laid out, and how did they keep the city clean?

topics.title: Trade, crafts and the end of the cities

learn.hook: Harappan beads have been found far away in Mesopotamia (in present-day Iraq). How did they travel so far?
points: Harappans traded with distant lands such as Mesopotamia, using boats, ships and bullock carts.
They made square seals, often of a soft stone called steatite, with animals and a script. Seals may have been used to mark goods.
The Harappan script has not yet been read (deciphered), so we still don't know what the signs say.
Crafts-people made beads of carnelian (a red stone), pots, bronze figures like the 'dancing girl', and used standard stone weights for trade.
After about 1900 BCE the cities slowly declined. Likely reasons include changes in climate, rivers like the Ghaggar-Hakra drying up, and floods. People moved to smaller villages.

example.q: Why might a Harappan trader have pressed a seal onto a clay tag tied to a sack of goods?
steps: Seals carried a picture and some signs.
Pressing a seal on wet clay left a mark that showed who sent the goods.
This helped keep track of goods in trade.
example.answer: To mark the goods, showing where or whom they came from.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers today use stamps, labels and barcodes on packets, a little like Harappan seals.

items.text: Harappan seals were often made of ___.
Beads were made of a red stone called ___.
The Harappan script has not been ___ yet.

quiz.q: With which faraway region did the Harappans trade?
quiz.explain: Harappan beads and seals have been found in Mesopotamia, in present-day Iraq.
quiz.mistake: Picks a far-off continent with no ancient link

quiz.q: What were Harappan seals mostly made of?
quiz.explain: Most seals were carved from steatite, a soft stone that is easy to carve.
quiz.mistake: Thinks seals were made of precious metal

quiz.q: Why can we not yet read Harappan writing?
options: The script has not been deciphered
quiz.explain: Scholars have many seals with signs but have not yet worked out the script.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Harappans had no writing

quiz.q: What were carnelian beads?
options: Red stone beads made by Harappan crafts-people
quiz.explain: Carnelian is a red stone; Harappans cut and polished it into fine beads.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what carnelian is

quiz.q: Why did the Harappans use standard stone weights?
options: To measure goods fairly in trade
quiz.explain: Weights of fixed sizes helped traders measure goods correctly.
quiz.mistake: Does not link weights with trade

quiz.q: Which famous bronze figure was found at Mohenjo-daro?
quiz.explain: The small bronze 'dancing girl' shows the skill of Harappan metal workers.
quiz.mistake: Guesses an object without knowing

quiz.q: After about what time did Harappan cities slowly decline?
quiz.explain: The cities slowly declined after about 1900 BCE.
quiz.mistake: Confuses BCE with CE

quiz.q: Which is a likely reason for the decline of Harappan cities?
options: Changes in climate and rivers drying up
People moved to big modern cities
quiz.explain: Changes in climate, drying rivers such as the Ghaggar-Hakra and floods are likely reasons.
quiz.mistake: Picks an impossible modern reason

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Did Harappan people only stay at home, or did they trade with other lands?'
teach.praise: Super! Harappans traded with lands like Mesopotamia, used seals and standard weights, and made beautiful carnelian beads!
teach.nudge: Which faraway land did they trade with, and what did they use to mark their goods?
